scope: metadata-first ZIP/folder review, import plans/layout and shared publication path checks
checks: ZIP metadata inspection uses two bounded range reads with no content inflation; reviewed keep/strip layouts and manifest preserve explicit source/destination paths

folder metadata admission precedes content reads, reserved Studio metadata is explicitly listed/omitted, exact binary/BOM/CRLF/64-bit source survives ZIP preparation and cancellation stops before upload
duplicate/case/Unicode aliases, file/directory conflicts, world paths, mixed root removal and oversized files refuse using tiny metadata cases

actual PackStore import/export preserves three exact files and excluded/unknown content, existing packs remain intact, corrupt content and aliases reject before publication, staged cleanup and concurrent create/import locking pass

controlled import UI previews/export plans before upload, binds confirmed name/layout/original ZIP, cancels folder preparation on close, avoids navigation after an already submitted closed import, and suppresses late inspection publication
actual app post-import handoff refuses navigation when a successor dialog opens and reports committed success separately from a listing/open failure
limits: Three tiny pack files, one omitted metadata record, a synthetic range-only file extent with no large payload, actual local PackStore and controlled modal/application hosts. ZIP inspection is preliminary metadata only; the server independently checks actual header/decompression/CRC/path content before staging. Input limits remain 20,000 entries / 64 MiB per file / 256 MiB archive-expanded payload; central-directory inspection admits 32 MiB and browser review pages contain 32 rows. Selected-folder ZIP preparation is in memory and cancellable between file reads; full heap/large-input performance and real browser Blob/file/folder/layout/upload/network qualification remain pending. App create/import share a pack-name lock within one server instance; direct external filesystem writers/multiple server processes remain outside that coordination. No native build/generation, registry/state sweep, GPU work, broad suite or GitHub workflow.
